subject: Decision Making
title: Irving Janis Discovers Groupthink
description: A quick, practical guide to Irving Janis Discovers Groupthink.

hook.text: Psychologist Irving Janis studied the Bay of Pigs fiasco and found that smart people made terrible decisions together.

buildup.text: Kennedy's advisors were brilliant individually. But in the group, dissent was suppressed and risks were minimized.

discovery.text: Janis coined groupthink: the tendency of cohesive groups to prioritize harmony over honest analysis of alternatives.

twist.text: The same team that failed at Bay of Pigs succeeded during the Cuban Missile Crisis. Kennedy changed the group process.

climax.text: Groupthink is not about stupid people. It is about smart people in a bad process. Fix the process, fix the decisions.

punchline.text: Smart people, terrible choice. Groupthink is a process failure.

quiz.question: What is groupthink?
options: A cohesive group prioritizing harmony over honest analysis of alternatives
